ruling.reasoning: The trip is a fixed-quote RydeX fare: $30.99 comprising base $3.90 + distance $19.67 (13.95 km) + time $5.95 (22.9 min) + platform $1.47 [F6], and the billed distance (14.0 km) does not exceed the optimal route (14.0 km) [F4]. Under RD-2 the non-metered branch refunds only ERP/toll actually incurred or undisclosed post-trip add-ons; a longer driven path does not change a fixed quote, and the record shows no toll or extra item in the fare breakdown [F6], so the refundable amount is $0 and the outcome is no_action, while the RD-1 obligation breach is recorded [RD-1][RD-2]. The single off-route segment 22:33–22:42 (+4.08 km, up to 1450 m off the optimal route) is not a detour if the rider agreed to that route before it started [F3][RD-5]. At 22:29 the driver asked "Jam on Central Expressway is building up ahead, can I go round via Lower Delta Road?" and the rider replied "Sure, go ahead." [F7][F8], both timestamped in a complete 2-message record [F9]; the reply precedes the 22:33 segment start and names the route the driver asked to take, so the segment is exempt as a rider-agreed route change under RD-5. The driver's later statement of verbal agreement is a claim, not consent [F10], but the chat itself supplies the consent needed [RD-5]. The speed-band record on the replaced stretch (Central Expressway band 2 during 22:06–22:33) cannot independently exempt the segment, since no traffic incident was recorded on the route during the trip window [F11][F14][RD-4]. RD-6 does not apply: the driver has no upheld route dispute in the last 90 days (route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0) [F17], so no account flag arises even though RD-1 was breached [RD-6]. On the RD-3 branch, no stop was measured in the segment and the rider's message did not name a place for a stop, so RD-3 gives no separate exemption; the segment rests on RD-5 alone [F7][F8][RD-3]. The amount is null because no refund arises on a fixed fare with no refundable add-on [F4][F6][RD-2].
